title: Trump Orders America to “Love Me” and Sends Us Taxpayers the Bill
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Trump Orders America to “Love Me” and Sends Us Taxpayers the Bill

Taxpayers are footing the bill for a Fox “News” ad glorifying the president, as lawmakers question whether federal law has been crossed…

Actual Article Body:
Share

Turn on Fox “News” at night this week and you’ll see something no American has ever seen before but Russians would immediately recognize.

Images of the American president flash across the screen while a singer repeats the words “love me” over and over, Trump’s voice promises to defeat “communism, socialism and Marxism,” UFC boss Dana White calls him “the toughest, most resilient person that I’ve ever met,” and then, at the bottom of the screen, six words appear:

“Paid for by the U.S. government.”

Mediaite has confirmed that the ad ran through three shows on Fox but the White House says it’s all fine because it’s a “public service announcement” that’s “educational and unapologetically patriotic” and “clearly not political” because “the President is not on the ballot.”

The singer, JMSN, says he never authorized his song for “ANY political agenda or campaign.” Even Republican Senator Thom Tillis said using taxpayer dollars like this “feels like Viktor Orbán” and John Kennedy of Louisiana said he doesn’t “like to see politicians use public money to pay for their own campaign ads.”

Even more astonishing, this bit of state-run, taxpayer-funded propaganda that promises to destroy communism aired the same day Trump was rolling out a literal red carpet for Xi Jinping, an actual communist.

We’re finally reaching Full Putin here in America; with the “paid for by…” admission, this is the latest and most blatant example of Trump using the property, money, and machinery of the United States government to build a personal cult around himself and his billionaire buddies.

This pathetic, strongman-style self-aggrandizement isn’t new for Trump, of course, other than the admission in black-and-white type that our tax dollars are funding it.

— Back in 2020, Trump demanded his signature be prominent on the pandemic stimulus checks Congress appropriated to keep the economy afloat. — When puppy-killer Kristi Noem budgeted $200 million for ads featuring her on horseback, she told a crowd at CPAC that Trump told her, “I want the first ad, and I want you to thank me.” — Three-story banners of Trump’s face went up on the Agriculture, Labor, and Justice Department buildings in Washington, and Senator Adam Schiff’s office documented at least $50,000 in taxpayer contracts to pay for them. — The State Department put his portrait and signature inside our U.S. passports, the first living president ever to appear there. — The Treasury is now minting a gold-colored dollar coin with his face on it, even though federal law says only a dead person’s likeness can appear on our currency and the bipartisan coin advisory committee refused to review it. — His name was slapped on the Kennedy Center, on TrumpRx.gov, on the Palm Beach airport, on “Trump accounts,” and on a “Trump class” of battleships, among other things. Now he’s reportedly considering renaming Fords’ Theater where Lincoln was shot.

This nation’s Founders warned us, repeatedly, about exactly this sort of presidential self-aggrandizement.

When Congress wrote the very first Coinage Act in 1792, the Senate’s version called for the president’s head to appear on our money, just as the king’s did in England. George Washington, then the president, wanted no part of it, calling it a “monarchical act.”

He then used his Farewell Address to warn about future “cunning, ambitious, and unprincipled men” who would use the power, wealth, and levers of government to “subvert the power of the people.” As a result, the House version (which became law) of the Coinage Act specifically calls for “an impression emblematic of liberty” rather than a living president.

John Adams said we were to be “a government of laws, and not of men,” and Ben Franklin said he’d helped to create “a republic, if you can keep it.” Those men had put their lives on the line to create America, and now Trump is committed to destroying this republic and replacing it with a form of government like his mentor and owner, Putin, has creat
